prompt:
Use case: precise-object-edit
Edit target: the attached King of Spades trial playing card.
User feedback: the card is suitably minimal but the centre no longer looks recognisably like a king. Fix that balance.
Preserve the portrait card proportions, plain opaque off-white background, clean sans-serif K and correct spade corner indices, generous margins, and monochrome palette.
Replace only the central generic circle-and-rectangle pictogram and its extra bottom spade with an elegant RECOGNISABLE double-ended KING portrait, occupying about 40 percent of the card width and 50 percent of its height. Make a human king in profile: a distinctive three-point crown, a forehead and long clear nose formed by a precise negative-space silhouette, one tiny eye, a short squared beard, simple neck and a single geometric shoulder shape. The crown should rest naturally on the head. Mirror the bust with 180-degree rotational symmetry at the waist, as on an actual court card.
Illustration style: contemporary high-end editorial graphic design, flat black and ivory shapes. A few confidently drawn lines and masses, roughly six to eight simple shapes per king. A face readable instantly at phone size. The hair may be one plain solid shape, the beard one simple shape. No circles pretending to be heads. No chess-piece symbols. Do not make it a generic icon of a person.
Minimalism: no hair strands, fabric patterns, jewellery, sceptre, weapons, hands, ornamental frame, texture, gradients or tiny decoration. Enough human facial character to immediately say KING, but considerably simpler than conventional playing-card portraits. Balance the portrait's small black areas with open white space. Portrait should be clear and elegant, not cartoonish or cute.
Ensure the whole canvas has a solid opaque white background, never transparent or black. Exactly one finished card, no external labels or additional text.
